title: SEC-CARRIER-PATH-001 · The host-supplied session id reaches the loop-guard state filename unvalidated, and a value with `../` rewrites the user's own ~/.claude/settings.json
description: src/guards/loop.ts:20-22 builds its state path as join(home(), "cache", "loop", `${sessionId()}.json`) with sessionId() returning the surface's session_id verbatim (src/env.ts:97-110, adopted at src/chain/mod.ts:143) or AI_ENG_SESSION. A session id of "../../../.claude/settings" makes path.join normalise out of ~/.ai-engineering/cache/loop into $HOME, so the first PreToolUse in a governed repo overwrites the user's real ~/.claude/settings.json with loop state JSON ({"recent":[...],"failures":{},"denials":{}}) — their hooks, permissions and env are gone. The same write reaches ~/.codex/hooks.json (the Codex machine carrier) or ~/.ai-engineering/machine.json. This is the identical defect the milestone's work point 07 names ("el session_id entra crudo en la ruta: traversal si se arregla a medias") and fixed in the verdict cache (src/chain/mod.ts:156 hashes it); the loop guard, which runs on every PreToolUse and every PostToolUse (TABLE matcher /^.*$/), was missed, and the same unpatched code is shipped inside the in-process bundle that runs in OMP/OpenCode/Pi (skills/.chain-bundle/ai-eng-chain.ts:728-747, bundle line 729). Reachability: the value comes from the payload's session_id (host-supplied) or from AI_ENG_SESSION, which src/env.ts:100 reads without any of the repository guard applied to AI_ENG_HOME at src/env.ts:13-21 — a repository-committed .env is merged into process.env by Bun in the process cwd (the exact route of the fixed LOGIC-003 finding), and the pi carrier sends no session_id at all (templates/plugin.pi.ts.tpl builds the payload without one), so on that surface the environment is the only source.
root_cause: stateFile in src/guards/loop.ts does not derive its filename from the session id, allowing a session id containing ../ to normalise out of the loop state directory and overwrite the user's own ~/.claude/settings.json (or the machine carrier) with loop-state JSON.
intended_behavior: The loop guard keeps per-session state under the home the install owns, at ~/.ai-engineering/cache/loop. The session id arrives from the host payload (or from AI_ENG_SESSION), so it is data and never a path component: the verdict cache, the sibling defect fixed in this same milestone, already derives the same value into a sha256 filename. State must be keyed by the session without ever being able to name a file the user owns.

returns the payload id or AI_ENG_SESSION verbatim — no charset, length or separator check
the state path is join(home(), cache, loop, sessionId() + .json), so a value with ../ normalises out of the loop directory and into HOME
writeFileSync writes the loop-state JSON at the traversed path on the first guarded PreToolUse, replacing whatever file that path names

conditions.description: the call happens inside a repo that declares itself (the malicious repo ships .ai-engineering/config.toml), so the gate lets the loop guard run
the chain call carries a session id the attacker influences: a host payload's session_id, or AI_ENG_SESSION set by a committed .env for a surface whose payload omits session_id (pi sends none)

execution.attacker_perspective: Read-only static audit: this session had no shell, so nothing was executed. The attacker is a repository author who wants the machine that runs their repo to lose a file, or an agent whose session id comes from a host payload it does not control. Every claim below was derived by reading the referenced lines; the commands are the exact reproduction a maintainer runs.
payloads: PreToolUse payload with tool_name Bash, tool_use_id d1 and session_id ../../../.claude/settings — the repo's own tests/adversarial/governance-gate.test.ts already drives ../../escaped through this same env.sessionId(), asserting only the verdict-cache filename
AI_ENG_SESSION=../../../.codex/hooks in a repository-committed .env, for a surface whose payload carries no session_id (templates/plugin.pi.ts.tpl builds the payload without one)
instructions: Static derivation, not an execution: src/env.ts sessionId() returns process.env.AI_ENG_SESSION or the payload id verbatim; src/chain/mod.ts adoptSession stores it; src/guards/loop.ts stateFile() interpolates it into a filename; path.join then normalises the ../ at write time and mkdirSync/writeFileSync follow the result.

Reproduction a maintainer runs on the pre-fix tree: printf %s PAYLOAD | bun src/chain/mod.ts PreToolUse inside a scratch governed repo, then cat ~/.claude/settings.json and ls ~/.ai-engineering/cache/loop.

Expected before the fix: ~/.claude/settings.json holds the loop-state object (recent, failures, denials) and the loop directory is empty. Expected after the fix: the loop directory holds one file matching the 32-hex .json name and the victim file is byte-identical to before.

The regression test in tests/adversarial/governance-gate.test.ts (named "the session id cannot walk out of the state directory the guard writes to") now asserts the derived filename, the sentinel preserved in the victim file, and a 32-hex name under the loop directory.

remediation.strategy: SEC-CARRIER-PATH-001 — FIXED. Disposition: fixed in src/guards/loop.ts after this run reported it; stateFile() now derives the filename with createHash("sha256").update(sessionId()).digest("hex").slice(0, 32), and skills/.chain-bundle/ai-eng-chain.ts is regenerated with the same derivation (bundle line 730). Regression test: tests/adversarial/governance-gate.test.ts, "the session id cannot walk out of the state directory the guard writes to". title: SEC-CARRIER-DESTROY-002 · installTemplateDir force-overwrites a pre-existing init.templateDir's own git hooks because shimState reports "empty" for a directory that holds someone else's hooks
description: src/floor/template.ts:44-57 only returns "ours" when one of the three shim names contains the marker and returns "theirs" solely on a read error; a template dir whose hooks/ holds the user's own pre-commit, commit-msg or pre-push therefore falls through to `return "empty"`. installTemplateDir then calls writeShims(previous, shimState(previous) === "empty") at src/floor/template.ts:101 with force=true, and the marker guard at src/floor/template.ts:66 is skipped entirely, so writeFileSync at :74 overwrites the user's hooks — the file's own comment two lines above says the opposite ("Never trample a hook a person wrote: ours only replace ours", "A hooks/ dir holding someone else's hooks is left alone entirely — the one thing this must never do is overwrite a person's hook to install ours") and the milestone's work point 06 promises "un templateDir que ya existia no se pisa". Reachable from `ai-eng init` (src/commands/init.ts:259) and `ai-eng update` (src/commands/update.ts:193) whenever init.templateDir was already set with a user hook. No test covers it: the only templateDir proof owns an empty GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL (scripts/proof-cli-ux.sh:145).
root_cause: shimState in src/floor/template.ts does not return theirs for a present hook that lacks our marker, allowing installTemplateDir to pass force=true to writeShims and overwrite a git hook the user wrote in a template directory they already owned.
intended_behavior: A template directory the user already had is joined, not taken over: our three shims go beside theirs, and a hooks/ directory holding someone else's hook is left alone entirely. Our marker is the only thing that says a hook is ours, so a hook without it is theirs by construction — which is what the function's own comment states and what the milestone's work point 06 promises.

a present hook whose body lacks the marker does not return theirs; the loop continues and the function falls through to empty
force is shimState(previous) === empty, so the wrong label becomes a force write
writeFileSync overwrites the person's hook because the marker guard is skipped when force is true

title: SEC-CARRIER-STATE-004 · The verdict cache is written into <repo>/cache/verdicts: unowned, un-swept, and staged into commits with absolute machine paths inside it
description: src/chain/mod.ts:156 puts the verdict cache at join(root, "cache", "verdicts", <hash>.json) — a new top-level directory in the user's worktree, outside the .ai-engineering state dir the lock owns. root_cause: the verdict-cache path in src/chain/mod.ts does not resolve inside the state directory the lock owns, allowing the cache — which stores the guard's own denial messages, absolute machine paths included — to land in an unowned repo-root directory that our own git add -A commits and that uninstall never removes.
intended_behavior: Generated state belongs to the install, not to the user's worktree: receipts live in .ai-engineering/receipts and are ignored, and the verdict cache holds the same class of machine-local data. Anything we write should stay inside the state directory, be ignored by git, and be pruned on uninstall.

title: SEC-CARRIER-STRIP-008 · A user's own $comment containing the word "ai-eng" is deleted by stripValue
description: src/install.ts:88 drops any `$comment` key whose string merely contains "ai-eng" — a substring test, while the marker rule for everything else is deliberately "the command ITSELF, not the word anywhere in a string" (src/install.ts:35-39). stripValue runs on the uninstall path and on update's swept repo carriers (src/surfaces/adapters.ts sweepMovedRepoCarriers for .claude/settings.json/.codex/hooks.json, src/commands/uninstall.ts:31-38), so a user file such as .claude/settings.json with `"$comment": "hooks managed by hand; ai-eng owns the guard entries"` loses that key on the next update or uninstall.
root_cause: stripValue in src/install.ts does not match our banner exactly, allowing a user's own comment string that merely contains ai-eng to be deleted from their settings file on update or uninstall.
intended_behavior: Our banner is the exact sentence we write, and our marker everywhere else is the command itself — never the word anywhere in a string. A hook or a comment of the user's that mentions the product is theirs and has to survive; the same file states that rule for hooks a few lines above.

trace.description: a $comment key whose string contains ai-eng is dropped, whatever the rest of the value says
the public strip path applies stripValue when a merged settings file is rewritten
uninstall rewrites the user's settings file without the comment, and update's sweep does the same to repo carriers
